scope: 8 open pull requests across acme · built from the raw diffs · nothing has been written to GitHub

across.label: Read together
across.text: ledger-app #418 and #421 both change how a plan upgrade is billed. Merge #421 first.

across.label: Repeats
across.text: Three of the five over the line change behavior their description does not mention.

prs.title: Fix proration on mid-cycle plan changes
prs.head: 4f1c2a9e8b7d6c5f4e3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e
prs.driver: Changes rounding in billing without saying so. A charge that is wrong stays made after a revert.
prs.ifWrong: Customers are overcharged by up to 1¢ on every mid-cycle change. A revert stops it, and charges already made stay made.
prs.proof: Three new tests cover the described rows. Nothing tests rounding.
prs.asked: Issue #415 asks for the downgrade fix. Rounding is not in it.

code.title: The code behind the two undescribed rows

read.judgment: Looks unintended. Keep Math.round, or round the difference once.
read.check: Is 1¢ on a same-price switch acceptable?
read.notExamined: Where a downgrade's credit is recorded.

prs.feedback: Bots raised 3 points. 2 fixed. 1 declined: "pin the rounding with a test", answered as out of scope.
prs.rest: 3 new tests, all matching the description.

prs.title: Refactor: rename formatCents to formatMinorUnits
prs.head: 9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b
prs.driver: Called a pure rename. It also adds a required database column and a new event, and neither comes back out with a revert.

text.none: No change a customer sees. Code that reads subscriptions now needs a value for the new required currency_exponent column, and other services can start listening for a plan.upgraded event.

prs.ifWrong: New subscriptions fail to save if any writer misses the column. The column and its backfilled data stay after a revert, and listeners to the new event keep expecting it.
prs.proof: The rename is covered by existing tests. Nothing tests the migration or the event.
prs.asked: Issue #402 asks for the rename only.

read.judgment: Split it. The rename can merge; the column and the event need their own pull request and a plan for existing rows.
read.check: Which services would subscribe to plan.upgraded?
read.notExamined: The backfill's run time on the production table.

prs.title: Unify HTTP client helpers and add retry backoff
prs.head: 1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c
prs.driver: Changes an exit code, which is a public contract, and deletes the one retry along with its test.
prs.ifWrong: Deploys fail more often on bad networks, and scripts that check for exit 1 behave differently. A release fixes it; scripts already written keep the old check.
prs.proof: CI passes, but the retry test was deleted with the code it covered.
prs.asked: Issue #127 asks for backoff on kit status only.

code.title: The code behind the two undescribed rows
The CI step that ran the deleted retry test

read.judgment: The codebase's one retry was crude, but deleting it is worse. Keep the retry and adopt the new backoff for it.
read.check: Does anything you run check for exit code 1?
read.notExamined: The other five commands that used the old helper.

prs.feedback: Bots raised 2 points. 1 fixed. 1 left open: "the 401 exit code changed".
prs.rest: The helper merge across 8 files, matching the description.

prs.title: Highlight the recommended plan
prs.head: c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00c0ffee00
prs.driver: A new look on a customer screen, which only a person can judge. One commit reverts it.

screens.sourceNote: The pull request links one screenshot that could not be opened.

path.step: Sees the plan cards: new badge, new buttons

prs.ifWrong: Plans look inconsistent with the rest of the app. One commit reverts it.
prs.proof: One test checks the badge text. Nothing checks the look.
prs.asked: Issue #430 asks for a badge. Restyling every plan's button is not in it.

read.judgment: DESIGN.md has one button, color from tokens, and no gradients. This departs on all three. If the gradient is wanted, change the design system first.
read.check: Look at the real screen at phone width.
read.notExamined: Who passes the recommended plan to this view.

prs.feedback: Bots raised 4 points. 3 fixed. 1 declined: "use the existing Button", answered as "the design calls for a gradient".
prs.rest: The badge markup and one test.

prs.title: Show the prorated amount on the plan card
prs.head: abcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcd
prs.driver: Shows a price on a customer screen and computes it a second way.
prs.ifWrong: The card shows a different amount from the invoice. One commit reverts it.
prs.proof: One test covers the Pro row. The current-plan row is untested.
prs.asked: Issue #433 asks for the amount on upgrades.

code.title: The code behind the undescribed row
lines: + const today = Math.round(((plan.price - current.price) * remaining) / days);

read.judgment: It recomputes proration instead of calling the billing helper, so the card and the invoice can disagree once ledger-app #421 lands.
read.check: Should the current plan show any amount at all?
